text:
maya: Heads up — seeing a ~3x jump in streaming keepalive failures out of eu-west2 since ~02:30 UTC. Synthetic WS checks have been flipping nodes unhealthy and causing extra capacity churn. Anyone else seeing this?

thomas: I see the alerts. Starting to dig into logs now. Is the spike aligned with deployment window?

li: no deploys at that time. Looks like client side short writes (499s) then LB closes. p95 connection lifetime jumped from 30s -> ~2m in the last hour on the grafana panel.

maya: here's the alert that fired: `blackbox_stream_ws_5xx_rate_high` — Prom rule shows rate over 1m > 0.5% for streaming routes. Also ops-bot posted the alert.

ops-bot: [ALERT] blackbox_stream_ws_5xx_rate_high fired (eu-west2) — 2026-03-18T02:33:12Z — affected: streaming-v2-prod. link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/alerts/1234 :rotating_light:

thomas: quick hypothesis — LB healthchecker/janitor is aggressively closing idle websockets during ephemeral NAT exhaustion. When sockets drop, our blackbox WS check sees it as an immediate failure and marks instance unhealthy, which triggers scale-up down/up. That churn could be amplifying the problem.

li: agreed. Two levers here: 1) probe sensitivity (increase grace / backoff), 2) infra fix (tweak LB keepalive / node snat pool). We should tune probes first to reduce noise.

maya: +1. Proposed probe changes for eu-west2 canary:
```
# blackbox exporter config snippet
modules:
  ws_streaming:
    prober: websocket
    timeout: 10s
    keepalive: true
    backoff: 3s
    retries: 2
    jitter: true
```
Increase timeout and add jitter/backoff so transient LB closures don't count as hard failures. Also sample only 1/10 of endpoints for full-frequency checks.

thomas: also recommend changing alert to require sustained window: from `increase over 1m` -> `sustained 5m` and require at least 3 instances affected. Example prometheus tweak:
```
expr: sum by(cluster)(rate(blackbox_stream_ws_errors_total[5m])) / sum by(cluster)(rate(blackbox_stream_ws_checks_total[5m])) > 0.01
for: 5m
```
That reduces flapping alerts.

li: question: what about embeddings endpoints? They use HTTP keepalives, different failure mode. Should we reduce their probe frequency instead of streaming? Cost-wise, streaming probes are heavier because they open a WS and can trigger model warmups (GPU work).

maya: good call. We should deprioritize non-critical embedding checks during peak and move them to sampling. Cost note: current probe fleet does ~250k streaming handshakes/day in eu-west2 -> approx $X in extra warmups. We should put a cap.

ops-bot: Incident created: I-20260318-027 — "eu-west2 streaming probe noise leading to churn". Assigned: maya, thomas.

thomas: Plan of action (short):
- Roll canary probe config in eu-west2 (sample 10%, jitter, retries=2)
- Update prometheus alert rule to 5m sustained + min-affected threshold
- Temporarily reduce embedding probe freq by 4x in eu-west2 during peak window
- Spawn ticket for infra: check SNAT exhaustion / LB keepalive defaults with cloud team

li: I'll draft the canary probe YAML and a patch for the alert rule. Maya, can you create the perf / cost calc for probe-induced warmups so we have numbers for the infra ticket?

maya: yep. Quick calc: ~250k handshakes/day * 0.002 GPU-warmups/handshake * avg-warmup-cost = estimate. I'll push numbers to the incident doc.

thomas: if the canary reduces alert noise, we'll push to all regions with staggered rollout. If not, we'll revert and focus on infra SNAT LB changes.

li: created PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/blackbox-configs/pull/482 — adds jitter+backoff + sampling for eu-west2. PTAL @maya @thomas

maya: reviewing now. quick review checkpoint: make sure `for: 5m` is present in alert and we add `min_affected_instances: 3` annotation. Also add note about cost impact in PR description.

ops-bot: NOTE: scheduled job `probe-rotation` will pick up config changes at 03:15 UTC; expected to deploy to eu-west2 canary shard only.

maya: thanks. I'll monitor graphs and update the incident doc. If we still see >1% error over 15m after canary, we escalate to infra team. :thumbsup:
